items.body:
[by Claude Code]

<!-- sglang-flaky-tracker:v1 -->

This issue tracks **flaky tests** and **recurring CI infrastructure failures** seen in NVIDIA `PR Test Base` / `PR Test Extra` runs while babysitting PRs with the `/sglang-pr-babysit` Claude Code workflow. It complements the CI tracker #17050. #17050 lists every failure signature by date. This issue records one row per flaky test, how often it was hit, and whether a rerun with no code change passed. Use it to pick the flakiest tests to debug.

A row is added only when triage found concrete evidence that the failure is **not caused by the PR** and **not a breakage on `main`**. PR-caused failures, `main` breakages, and uncertain cases are left out. Jobs that `github-actions[bot]` cancelled during a run of the maintainers' [Cancel Unfinished PR Runs](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/workflows/cancel-unfinished-pr-tests.yml) workflow are also left out. Those are deliberate cancels, not flakes or infrastructure failures.

## Format (v1)

Each row is one failure mode, keyed by **Test** (or **Job / step**) plus **Signature**. The same test failing with a different signature gets its own row.

- **ID**: `T<n>` for tests and `I<n>` for infra. IDs are never reused, even when a row is fixed or removed. Retired IDs: `I2`-`I10` (removed on 2026-10-08 because they were `Cancel Unfinished PR Runs` cancels).
- **Test**: `path::Class::method`, with the path relative to the repo root. Use `path` alone if the method is unknown.
- **Job / step**: the workflow job name, a slash, and the failing step or action.
- **Signature**: the exception type and message, with run-specific values (numbers, paths, hashes, ports, timestamps) replaced by `<N>`, `<PATH>`, and so on. At most about 100 characters.
- **Runner**: the runner label of the failing job, for example `1-gpu-h100` or `8-gpu-b300`.
- **Seen**: the number of failed job attempts recorded. Each failed attempt counts once, including a failed rerun.
- **Rerun passed**: `P/R`. `R` is the number of occurrences whose rerun has finished. `P` is how many of those reruns passed the same job with no code change.
- **First seen** / **Last seen**: UTC dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- **Recent jobs**: links to the last 3 failing jobs, newest first. Each link is labeled with its PR number.
- **Status**: `open`; `investigating (@user or #issue)`; or `fixed (#PR)`. If a `fixed` row fails again after the fix merged, it returns to `open` with `regressed after #PR`.

Rows are sorted by **Seen**, highest first. Ties are broken by **Last seen**, newest first.

Every occurrence is also posted as a comment on this issue. The comment starts with `<!-- sglang-flaky-occurrence:v1 -->` and holds the entry ID, PR, job link, why the failure is unrelated to the PR, and the rerun result. The comments are the append-only record, and the tables above are their summary.

## For debugging agents

Start from the top of each table. A test row with a high **Seen** count and a high **Rerun passed** ratio is a confirmed flake, and it is worth fixing or stabilizing. When you take a row, set its **Status** to `investigating (@you)`. When the fix merges, set it to `fixed (#PR)`.

items.body: issue:https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39700 base pr: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40179 ## Summary DeepSeek V4.1 consumer layers can share the same compressed KV storage, but sparse prefill currently dequantizes that storage into a BF16 workspace on every layer. Reuse the dequantized compressed KV within a forward to avoid repeated reads, dequantization, and workspace writes. ## Changes - Limit reuse to CP sparse BF16 prefill with compression ratios 1 and 2. - Keep separate workspaces per compression ratio. - Track validity by source layer and workspace address within the per-forward gather cache. - Refresh on producer execution, source changes, workspace reallocation, or a new forward. - Continue updating SWA and top-k inputs for every layer. This retains additional scratch memory for the separate workspaces. ## Validation - GPU regression tests cover shared sources, source updates, ratio interleaving, consecutive forwards, and workspace resizing. - All 16 short/long-context smoke-test outputs match the baseline. - In a six-step trace, compressed KV dequantization calls decrease from 228 to 24 (89.5% fewer). ### Performance DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on 8×B200 with PD disaggregation; prefill uses TP4/EP4, CP, BCG, MegaMoE, and DSpark. Results are medians of three unprofiled runs using the unchanged benchmark script, with 512 requests and an output length of 500, which is 60k unprefix cache of 64k all input length. ### precision gsm8k test result ## trace comparison before after --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39416278022](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39416278022) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39416278250](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39416278250) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39416278223](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39416278223)

items.body:
## Motivation

Add [InstantTensor](https://github.com/scitix/InstantTensor) as an optional high-performance loader for Safetensors checkpoints.

InstantTensor supports distributed weight loading and pipelined prefetching. This integration lets users select it with `--load-format instanttensor` while preserving SGLang's existing checkpoint discovery and model-loading flow.

It has already been integrated into several other projects, such as vLLM. https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/models/extensions/instanttensor/

## Modifications

- Add `instanttensor` to the supported load formats and CLI choices.
- Add an InstantTensor weight iterator based on `instanttensor.safe_open`.
- Require PyTorch's `cuda` device interface (including CUDA and ROCm). Reject unsupported devices during server-argument validation and at the iterator entry, before importing InstantTensor or accessing the current CUDA device.
- Reuse the existing Safetensors file discovery, shard index filtering, and checkpoint selection logic.
- Validate selected filenames at the InstantTensor iterator entry and reject non-`.safetensors` files before opening any checkpoint. Keep SGLang's existing discovery, download, cache, and pattern-priority behavior unchanged; unsupported selections fail explicitly rather than being automatically replaced.
- Pass SGLang's initialized device process group to InstantTensor for distributed loading.
- Support tuning through `--model-loader-extra-config`, including `buffer_size`, `chunk_size`, `io_depth`, and `backend`.
- Convert JSON backend names or ordered candidate lists to InstantTensor backend/policy enums. Skip SGLang's extra-config validation for InstantTensor and forward optional parameters without filtering. Pass filename, framework, device, process group, and `copy=True` explicitly; Python rejects duplicate arguments, and InstantTensor handles unsupported parameters and values.
- Add the optional `sglang[instanttensor]` dependency with `instanttensor>=0.1.9` to support these tuning options.
- Document core tuning options in the shared loader configuration table and link to InstantTensor for the latest options.
- Extend `SRTRunner` to select the load format and pass extra loader configuration in model-loading tests.
- Add focused CPU unit tests and a weekly single-GPU output-consistency test comparing Safetensors with explicitly configured InstantTensor loading.

### Configuration example

```bash
pip install "sglang[instanttensor]"

python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  --load-format instanttensor \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"backend":"URING","chunk_size":8388608,"io_depth":64}'
```

For the tuning options shown above, explicit non-null values override the corresponding `INSTANTTENSOR_*` environment variables. Omitted or `null` values retain InstantTensor's environment-variable and automatic defaults. Backend names are case-sensitive; an ordered list such as `{"backend":["URING","AIO"]}` selects the first available candidate. Additional optional parameters are forwarded unchanged, except that `filename`, `framework`, `device`, `process_group`, and `copy` cannot be overridden. Unsupported parameters, including generic loader settings such as `enable_multithread_load` and `num_threads`, are not silently dropped; they are left for InstantTensor to reject.

## Accuracy Tests

### CPU unit tests

All 8 InstantTensor-related CPU tests passed: 6 iterator tests and 2 server-argument hardware-validation tests.

These tests cover configuration forwarding (including `copy=True`), backend conversion, current-device and process-group selection, and rejection of unsupported filename suffixes at the iterator entry. Hardware tests accept the CUDA and ROCm platform classes, reject non-CUDA device types before importing InstantTensor or calling CUDA APIs, and check that other load formats remain usable with CPU devices. These are CPU-only interface tests, not ROCm hardware validation; real NCCL behavior is not covered by the mocks.

Related regression tests, CI registration checks, and applicable pre-commit checks also passed.

### GPU generation consistency

## Motivation

Model forwards can omit expert placement or the live token count, routing logical IDs against physical expert weights or processing padding as real tokens. Move those decisions into TopK and the active forward. Automatic padding also makes inactive routes reachable at EP1, so every affected consumer must skip their data, weights and expert addresses safely.

## Modifications

- Resolve placement per call and capture draft identity during construction. Align draft weight loading with identity routing, including in-range draft layer IDs; retain target placement-aware loading.
- Bind the prepared ForwardBatch across eager execution, graph capture/replay, CPU graphs and TBO children. Bind copied row/tail batches too. Decline DeepSeek row-tail capture when its MoE count is a separate GLOBAL buffer, using the existing eager path.
- Preserve lazy routing metadata until materialization. Keep the producing layer ID in TopKConfig, including piecewise reconstruction, so lazy LP conversion defaults to the correct solver while explicit overrides (including 0) still win. Keep the existing five-field tuple ABI. Reject logits-only consumers that cannot apply required remapping. Route DeepSeek graph admission through the same layer contract. Keep shared expert columns outside LP solving and routed-only remapping.
- Make Triton, Marlin, GGUF, W4AFP8 and Humming consumers honor inactive routes independently of EP, including NaN inputs/weights and poisoned intermediate buffers. Generic Marlin reuses its projection allocation, clearing the down view after activation consumes the up view; LoRA retains separate zeroed buffers.
- Support the published `sglang-kernel==0.4.10` GGUF provider with Python block-size selection, safe vector indices, masked inactive intermediates/contributions, and initialized MMQ slack metadata. Retain the AOT source fixes for future wheel builds.
- Initialize CUTLASS FP8 gather maps and use a masked Triton reduction that skips inactive data and weights. > Note: the first commit on this branch is the EAGLE verify-append hotfix from #44199 (watermarked EAGLE/EAGLE3 output is undetectable on main without it). This branch will be rebased to a single commit once #44199 lands.

DSPARK verifies a linear draft chain. Each verify row's context is the committed watermark tail followed by the earlier draft tokens, so the existing speculative selector applies with a lower-triangular chain mask. The DSPARK worker forces those rows before acceptance. After acceptance it records the accepted rows' contexts and appends the committed tokens to the ring.

**Design: verify-side forcing.**
- A forced row's target distribution is one-hot, so DSPARK's rejection-sampling accept — with or without block verification — emits exactly the watermarked token.
- Detection therefore follows the unchanged contract: no DSPARK-specific detector logic, single and dual key alike.
- Draft-side keyed sampling would raise acceptance, but it needs the selector inside DSPARK's folded draft graph and a cropped-vocabulary hash contract. It is left as follow-up given the measured cost below.

**Evidence** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8×H200, TP8/EP8, DSPARK block size 5):
- Detection: 40 essays × 512 tokens, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95. DSPARK median request z is 2.73 (16/40 at p < 1e-3) against 3.06 (18/40) without speculation on the same prompts; wrong key z 0.91. OFF: median z 0.21, 0/40.
- GSM8K-100 (temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95): 99% with 100% stop rate, both watermarked and not, 0 truncated, 0 errors.
- Throughput: bench_serving random 1024/512, c8, 100 prompts, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, six reps over two launches: TPOT +3.73%, output throughput −2.25%, accept length −3.27%.

**Also fixes** an EAGLE/NEXTN regression (#44199): the fused verify-commit path (#41175) skipped the watermark ring append, so watermarked EAGLE3 output on main is undetectable. On Qwen3-8B with EAGLE3 3/1/4, 0/40 requests reach p < 1e-3 before the fix and 40/40 after; tree 5/8/32 is also 40/40.

**Tests:**
- CUDA watermark selector/state suites, plus a DSPARK chain case. The case checks that rejection-sampling accept, with and without block verification, emits the forced tokens, and that the committed ring and context history equal those of non-speculative decode (22 passed total).
- Endpoint e2e `test_watermark.py` (5 passed).

Not covered: DSPARK with DP attention or PD disaggregation (PD stays rejected by validation). DFLASH stays rejected; its chain can reuse `force_speculative_chain` in a later PR.

items.title: [Perf] moe: Extend FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE autotune coverage to prefill chunks
items.body:
## Summary

**TL;DR: This PR enables sglang's startup autotune to tune FlashInfer's CUTLASS MoE kernel for prefill sizes too, not only for decode sizes.** sglang already autotunes this kernel (`cutlass_fused_moe`, FlashInfer's MoE kernel, not its attention backend) at startup, but each call tells FlashInfer to tune only up to its own token count. The startup run is one decode-sized batch, so only decode sizes get a tuned kernel configuration (tactic), and prefill chunks above that size run FlashInfer's untuned fallback tactic (its default kernel configuration). This PR gives FlashInfer one tuning range per server instead: the largest prefill batch the MoE layer sees (chunk size × attention data-parallel size, capped at 8192, FlashInfer's own default range for this call), so the same startup autotune also covers prefill. No new flag, kernel or extra pass. It applies on every GPU this kernel runs on (SM90, SM100, SM110, SM120), where it is the default MoE kernel of DeepSeek-V4.1/V4, Ling-3.0, Nemotron-H, gpt-oss and ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE models (which GPU for which model: Design notes), and to any other MoE model that runs on it. Other MoE kernels and the decode servers of prefill-decode (PD) disaggregation are unchanged. Measured on H200 (SM90).

- **Performance** (H200): faster prefill on all seven MoE models measured (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5, Ling-3.0, gpt-oss-20b, GLM-5.3-Flash, MiniMax-M3, Gemma-4): TTFT (time to first token) for 8k-token prompts **30.3–57.8% lower** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: 573.9 → 400.0 ms, **30.3%**), for 32k-token prompts **23.0–52.8% lower**, prefill throughput **43.4–143.4% higher**; decode ITL (inter-token latency) unchanged on the three models measured for it. It complements open PR #42736 (an extra startup tuning pass): with both, 8k-token TTFT on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is **24.7% lower** than with #42736 alone.
- **Accuracy:** unchanged by design (only the tile configuration, or tactic, of the same GEMM changes); GSM8K on all seven models and the DeepSeek-V4-Flash CI GSM8K test stays within the 95% noise range (−0.83 to +0.15 points on the seven models).
- **Cost:** a longer startup autotune when no saved results exist: 41–42 → 176–177 s on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 8×H200 (server ready 153–154 → 288–289 s), 116 → 604 s on Ling-3.0-flash, and 4–26 s more on the other five models. Saved results are reused on one GPU, but multi-GPU servers currently re-tune at every start; `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` turns the startup autotune off. Each GPU has 0.4–1.2 GiB (0.3–0.9% of an H200) less free memory while the server runs, mostly the buffer FlashInfer keeps for timing tactics at startup, now sized for the prefill chunk instead of the decode batch; the KV cache size is unchanged. PD decode servers pay nothing.

## Motivation

sglang runs FlashInfer's autotune at startup (#12306, on by default since #14357). For `cutlass_fused_moe`, FlashInfer keeps one tactic per token-count bucket (powers of two up to 256, then larger steps up to 8192: 21 buckets) and tunes every bucket up to the caller's `tune_max_num_tokens`; the same value also decides which bucket a call uses. Both sglang call sites (the `flashinfer_cutlass` runner, used for BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 experts, and the CUTLASS path of `flashinfer_mxfp4`, used for MXFP4 experts) pass `next_power_of_2(x.shape[0])`, which dates from #7327, before the startup autotune existed. This has two effects:

1. **Prefill runs an untuned tactic.** The startup batch is decode-sized, one token per request up to the request limit (256 tokens on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 138 on Nemotron-3.5-Lightning, 4096 on gpt-oss-20b), so nothing above that size is tuned: an 8k-token chunk maps to bucket 8192 and gets FlashInfer's fallback tactic. The server log shows nothing, because sglang sets FlashInfer's logger to ERROR.
2. **The tactic depends on earlier requests.** Every `cutlass_fused_moe` call that runs Python code (the startup autotune, CUDA graph capture, and every serving forward that is not a CUDA graph replay) first calls `MoERunner.refine_tuning_config(tune_max_num_tokens)`. That method is wrapped in `functools.lru_cache` and rebuilds FlashInfer's class-wide bucket list only the first time it sees a value, so a call with a value seen before keeps the list built for the latest new value. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64`, the first decode batch of 65–128 requests while serving runs without a CUDA graph and rebuilds the list for 128 tokens (a short prompt of a new size likewise rebuilds it, for its own size); later prefill chunks of an already-seen size, such as every 8k-token chunk after the first, then run the 128-token bucket's tactic, because a list built for 128 tokens ends at bucket 128 and every larger call falls into that last bucket.

flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5625 was filed by an sglang user who hit both effects serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 4×H100 with `flashinfer_mxfp4`. One value for the whole server, computed from its configuration and used by every call, as large as the largest prefill batch (up to 8192 tokens), removes both.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py`** -- the new `_cutlass_moe_tune_max_num_tokens(num_tokens)` gives both `cutlass_fused_moe` calls their `tune_max_num_tokens`: `min(prefill chunk size × attention DP size, 8192)`, with the chunk size (`--chunked-prefill-size`, or `--max-prefill-tokens` when chunked prefill is off) read the way `flashinfer_autotune.py` already does (`max_prefill_buffer_tokens() or get_schedule().max_prefill_tokens`). PD decode servers keep `next_power_of_2(num_tokens)`.
- **`test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_swiglu_params.py`** (CPU suite) -- new `TestCutlassMoeTuneMaxNumTokens`. With the kernel stubbed, it checks at both calls that token counts 1, 257, 777, 2048, 4097, 8192 and 16384 map to a bucket the startup autotune tunes, in five server configurations, and that PD decode servers keep the per-call value. 60 of its 80 sub-cases fail on main.

Design notes:

- Where this kernel is the default MoE path: on SM90 and SM120, DeepSeek-V4.1/V4 and Ling-3.0 (MXFP4 experts, through `flashinfer_mxfp4`) and BF16/FP8 Nemotron-H (`flashinfer_cutlass`); on SM120 also gpt-oss and ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE models, the latter on SM110 too since #41765. On SM100 no model uses it by default (`flashinfer_mxfp4` runs a TRT-LLM kernel there). Any other MoE model reaches it with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass` (BF16, ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4) or `flashinfer_mxfp4` (MXFP4).
- DP attention: sglang splits `--chunked-prefill-size` across the DP ranks, and the MoE layer runs on the tokens gathered from all of them, so the largest batch the MoE layer sees is each rank's chunk × the DP size, which is the `--chunked-prefill-size` the user set.
- The 8192 cap is a choice, not a limit on chunk size: it is FlashInfer's own default range for this call, and chunks larger than 8192 tokens still run, using bucket 8192's tactic, which in a one-layer test with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's MoE shape is as fast as a tactic tuned for each larger size (One MoE call, under Experimental Results); tuning beyond 8192 would only lengthen startup. Omitting the argument would also give one value, but PD decode servers and servers with smaller chunks would then tune sizes they never use.
- Servers whose startup decode batch is above 8192 tokens (for example attention DP 8 with the default request limit) tune fewer buckets than main and start faster, at no MoE run-time cost: main cannot use those larger buckets at run time either (item 2), and in a one-layer test bucket 8192's tactic is about as fast as each size's own tactic at 12288–32768 tokens (One MoE call, under Experimental Results).

## Motivation

Depends on #31700.

DeepSeek-V4 Two-Batch Overlap (TBO) with DP attention,
`moe_a2a_backend=none`, and attention tensor parallelism greater than one
applies full-TP variable-length collectives to tensors replicated within each
attention-TP group. Treating those replicas as independent shards corrupts the
gather and combine layouts and produces invalid model output.

This change gives each full-TP rank one shard of its replicated DP-local tensor
and reconstructs the DP-local result across the attention-TP group after the
combine.

## Modifications

- Derive and validate DP-local token counts and full-TP shard counts for each

- Shard replicated hidden states and input IDs across attention-TP ranks before

- Reduce-scatter the MoE output into one shard per full-TP rank, then

- Compute the replicated TP1 shared expert on the DP-local tensor and add it

items.title: [Spec] DSPARK: hand the overlap readback a snapshot of the folded accept, not views (#42465)
items.body:
## Motivation

#42465: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` and HiCache `write_through` deadlocks across TP ranks. With `SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER=1` the ranks diverge on `cache_finished_req ... owned_kv_len` by 1-2 tokens, so each rank inserts a different prefix and the write-through backups no longer line up.

The mechanism, as @divyvasal found: the folded accept runs inside the target-verify CUDA graph and writes fixed epilogue buffers (`commit_lens_buf`, `out_tokens_buf`, ...) that the next replay rewrites. `accept_and_finalize(folded_accept=True)` returned `read_accept(bs)`, i.e. views of those buffers, and the DSPARK worker put them into `GenerationBatchResult.accept_lens` / `next_token_ids`. Under the overlap scheduler `_copy_result_to_cpu` issues that readback on `copy_stream` after `copy_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)` and then launches forward N+1 without waiting for the copy. When the copy engine is busy, for example behind the write-through device-to-host copy of a ~540K-token prefix, the readback runs after replay N+1 and reads step N+1's accept lengths. Each rank races on its own, so ranks commit different token counts. The in-graph accept is broadcast from rank 0, so the ranks agree on the device; only the host readback diverges.

## Modifications

- `dspark_verify.py`: `DsparkVerifyEpilogue.snapshot_accept(bs)` returns clones of the six accept buffers. The clones are made on the forward stream right after the replay, so stream order pins them to step N, and `async_d2h`'s `record_stream` keeps them alive until the readback has run. `TargetVerifyExecutor.accept_and_finalize` returns the snapshot on the folded path. `read_accept` keeps returning views, because the in-graph `_accept` writes through them (`build_accept_outs(..., out=self.read_accept(bs))`).
- `scheduler.py`: comment in `_copy_result_to_cpu` updated; no behavior change (the DSpark inline copy under Confidential Computing is kept as validated).
- Cost: six small device-to-device copies per verify step on the forward stream, no extra stream sync.

### Relation to #42812

#42812 clones inside `read_accept`. That was right at its base (264d1c20, 2026-10-06), where `_accept` wrote the buffers directly. Since #43790 (2026-10-12) `_accept` passes `read_accept(bs)` as its in-graph destination, so cloning there makes the graph write into throwaway clones and the static buffers never update. On today's main the existing `test_dspark_accept_tail.py::test_graph_accept_matches_eager_greedy` fails with #42812's hunk applied (4 subtests). This PR keeps the alias where the graph needs it and snapshots where the views escape. @shanemort1982 reported the same breakage on #42812 on 2026-10-19 and proposed the same split (views accessor as the write target, clones for the reader); this PR keeps `read_accept` as the views so the in-graph call site is unchanged and adds `snapshot_accept` for the reader.

## Accuracy / tests

- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dspark_accept_tail.py::TestFoldedAcceptSnapshot` (CPU): the folded `accept_and_finalize` output must not alias the epilogue buffers and must keep its values after the buffers are rewritten. Fails on main (`AssertionError: True is not false : correct_len`), passes with the fix. The existing parity case still passes.
- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dspark_overlap_readback_streams.py` (1-GPU): deterministic replay of the interleaving with real streams and `async_d2h`: a spin kernel on copy_stream stands in for the busy copy engine, forward_stream rewrites the buffers for step N+1; views read step N+1 (the hazard), the snapshot reads step N. On an H200 (main 5cbe2371a5 + this change): both cases pass; against the pre-fix `dspark_verify.py` the view case still reproduces the hazard and the snapshot case fails. The full `test/registered/unit/spec/` sweep passes (308 tests, 176 subtests). Re-run on 2026-10-19 against main 8e7601ae4a: same outcomes, sweep 311 passed, 182 subtests.
- Not reproduced end to end: the hang needs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4 GPUs (TP4); @divyvasal validated the equivalent clone at 43.1M tokens per replica with 0 rank divergence in #42812.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation: not applicable.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results: not applicable (no numerics change; six tiny D2D copies per verify step).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.body:
## Motivation

Vision-enabled DeepSeek-V4.1 checkpoints route text-only requests through CUDA `vision_topk()` too. Outside MegaMoE, that path skips ordinary TopK finalization: expert-distribution counts stay empty and nonidentity EPLB placement does not reach the physical-expert dispatch boundary.

Fixes #42188.

## Modifications

- Keep device-side, per-token text/image correction-bias selection and finalize CUDA VL routes through ordinary TopK's capture, expert mapping, shared-slot and recorder path.
- Pass existing expert-location dispatch information through both normal and dual-stream DeepSeek MoE call sites.
- Retain fused packed output when finalization preserves its IDs and weights; use the standard unpacked result after remapping.
- Mask padding after shared-slot rewrites. Preserve the existing non-CUDA and MegaMoE behavior.

No modality-admission synchronization, public option or dependency is added.

## Accuracy Tests

Head: `1c598de9d1757973d74d02b1360cda328b3f152e`, based on `e5dc10e73b0c4ccae7a9c4f454411b399e83a4f0`.

The validation below was completed before the test-only deletion commit `1c598de9d1`. That commit removes the new VL routing regression file; both runtime implementation files remain byte-identical to the validated `b1ce87b364` revision. This PR now contains only the two implementation files.

The removed H200 regression had 7 passing methods at `b1ce87b364`. On unmodified `6fe630ae14`, it produces 12 failing subtests and one error. It covers real per-layer counting, text/image bias selection, nonidentity static/dynamic expert mapping, packed output, shared scaling and per-rank slots, padding, empty rows, CUDA graph input refresh, and both actual MoE entry points with a small numerical expert boundary. Existing MegaMoE regressions (2) and CPU multimodal graph regressions (2) also pass.

Matched checkpoint A/B: `6fe630ae14` versus `3860e0f414`, 8xH200, TP8/EP4/DP1, local DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 snapshot, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1. The implementation and validation test were byte-identical after rebasing to `b1ce87b364`; the test file is removed in the current head. A full 5,749-file Python-tree audit finds only the two intended implementation files differ between the A/B arms.

| Check | Baseline | Candidate |

| Text/image-color/OCR functional requests | 19/19 | 19/19 |
| Logical expert-count total, each of 3 rounds | 0 | 5,222,400 |
| Official sgl-eval 0.1.3 GSM8K | 1282/1319 (97.19%) | 1281/1319 (97.12%) |
| GSM8K errors / truncations | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Recorder rounds use 32 requests x 64 output tokens. Every one of 40 layers records 130,560 selections, matching `32 * (22 + 64 - 1) * top6 * 8 replicated ranks` under the existing stat-reduction convention. Both dump replicas agree and are not summed together. GSM8K uses temperature 0, seed 0, C32, max 2048 tokens, thinking off; 1315/1319 parsed answers agree, with two baseline-only and one candidate-only correct results. This is a finite task evaluation, not exact output equivalence.

Real attention-DP2 validation requires the existing padding fixes from [#40424](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40424), adapted in a separate validation copy. Unpatched main reaches that PR's `Repeat.cu` padded-row assertion during startup; the unchanged helper reproduces it on H200 with crash-safe input dumps. Those dependency fixes are outside this PR.

With that explicit dependency, TP8/EP4/attention-DP2 eager and BCG each pass 49/49 requests: text -> mixed text/image -> text, plus an idle peer. During the mixed phase, requests are directed to text-only DP0 and image-bearing DP1; scheduler logs confirm the routing. The only prefill graph bucket is 256 tokens. Actual graph-pass deltas are 15/14/15, including six image-bearing DP1 passes. All 48 paired answers agree ignoring three color-word capitalization differences. Both DP2 arms disable decoder bounded replay, which currently rejects attention TP4/DP2.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same fixed-source TP8/EP4/DP1 A/B: speculation and HiCache off, context 65536, memory fraction 0.70, chunked prefill 2048. Each run uses 128 requests, C32, exactly 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, seed 42, 16 warmup requests and a cache flush. Every measured request succeeds with the stated token lengths.

items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] DSA: Pick any divisor of the tile count for the TileLang sparse decode split
items.body:
## Summary

**TL;DR: This PR lets the CUDA TileLang FP8 sparse decode group a query's top-k tiles by any divisor of the tile count, not only by halving it, when the resulting blocks still fill the GPU. For GLM-5.3-Flash, whose 2051-wide top-k pads to 66 tiles, decode at 16 requests per GPU with MTP now splits each query into 6 partial groups instead of 33.** Fewer groups means fewer partial results to write and merge. Top-k widths with a power-of-two tile count (2048, as in DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 to GLM-5.2) get the same split as before, and ROCm keeps its current search.

- **Performance** (GLM-5.3-Flash on H200, FP8 KV cache): with attention DP8 and MTP, the sparse decode attention kernels run **1.36× faster** per call (27% less GPU time), and steady decode throughput is **2.5% higher** at 128 concurrent requests and **1.2% higher** at 64. Per kernel call, across 8 to 64 heads per GPU and 4 to 200 query rows, this PR is **8–27% faster wherever it changes the split and never slower**. With TP8 (8 heads per GPU), the decode step is up to 1.2% shorter at 2 to 8 concurrent requests and the same at 1 and 16.
- **Accuracy:** **unchanged** end to end: GSM8K is 97.04% with this PR and 97.35% on main, within one standard error (0.44 points), and the MTP accept length is the same. Larger groups round the FP8 softmax probabilities more coarsely, so the kernel error rises at the new splits, but it stays below the error of the splits main already uses for 66 or more rows.
- **Cost:** with an empty TileLang kernel cache, the first start takes about 35 s longer to compile the kernels for the new group sizes; later starts take the same time as main. Choosing the group size is a short integer loop on the host.

## Motivation

#42957 added the FP8 KV cache to the TileLang DSA backend on CUDA through the partial + combine path of `tilelang_sparse_fwd`, which serves both prefill and decode. That path splits each query's top-k KV tiles into `ni / inner_iter` groups, computes one partial result per group, and merges the partial results with a combine kernel. `_pick_inner_iter` picks `inner_iter`, the number of tiles per group, and tries only `ni, ni // 2, ni // 4, ...`. With a top-k width of 2048 (64 tiles), these halvings are exactly the divisors of `ni`, so nothing is lost.

GLM-5.3-Flash's indexer appends up to 3 not-yet-pooled tail tokens (KPool) to the 2048 selected ones. `_forward_tilelang` pads the 2051 columns to the next multiple of 64, 2112, which is 66 tiles of 32 on CUDA. Halving 66 gives 33, 16, 8, 4 and 2, and only 33 and 2 divide 66.

The search also keeps enough blocks to fill the GPU: `seq * ni / inner_iter >= cu * block_per_cu`, where `seq` is the number of query rows in the call and `block_per_cu` is 1 on CUDA. On a 132-SM GPU this allows at most `seq / 2` tiles per group. So for 4 to 65 query rows the search falls back to 2 tiles per group: 33 partial results per query, each written out and read back by the combine kernel, although 11 tiles per group (6 groups) fits the same limit at 32 rows. With MTP (multi-token prediction) each decoding request contributes 2 query rows with one draft token, so 16 requests per GPU give 32 rows.

This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44994
* __->__ #44993
* #44991
* #44480

## Motivation

A MoE quantization method can execute on Triton while the requested backend remains FlashInfer or AITER. Dispatch, weight preparation and routing must follow the layer that actually executes. Backend identity also does not prove that a native router implements the model's routing policy: AUTO-resolved NVFP4 must preserve custom routing and renormalization.

## Modifications

- Quantization methods expose their effective execution backend, including wrapped methods, secondary runners and direct kernels. FusedMoE binds dispatch, expert-ID layout, transport payloads, post-load transforms and each model router to that contract.
- TRT-LLM in-kernel routing requires a declared policy matching the model's scoring, grouping, bias, renormalization, custom-router and shared-slot behavior. Other routers retain materialized STANDARD output. Explicit `Default` enum value 0 remains a real policy, distinct from an unspecified selector.
- TRT-LLM routed adapters consume materialized weights without renormalizing them again. Unsupported materialized per-tensor FP8 input fails before the kernel; an undeclared per-tensor router retains the Triton fallback and its compatible weight layout.
- Materialized TRT-LLM routes include the routed factor for every effective quantization method, including compressed-tensors FP8/NVFP4 schemes. Grouped/biased fallback producers apply the factor independently of renormalization while preserving shared contributions. Native routers still apply their own factor once. Ordinary loaders zero untouched padded weight tails, including repeated loads.
- Preserve model-wide DP layout for fallback payloads, gate AITER-specific transforms on the effective backend, and keep weight-only helpers with no runner valid. Binding is idempotent for the same contract and rejects conflicting reuse. The gfx1250 W4A8 internal router rejects unsupported expert sharding.

Equivalent native policies are declared for normalized MiMoV2 grouped sigmoid/bias, BailingMoE grouped sigmoid/bias or plain softmax, and Cohere2 sigmoid. Other configurations remain materialized. DeepSeek's logits-only dual-stream graph requires a BYPASSED router even when this PR is used independently.

Llama4 FP8 explicitly selects the model's top-1 sigmoid native policy. Gemma4 NVFP4 materializes its model router so selected-expert softmax weights retain the learned per-expert multiplier. These change behavior relative to the earlier native defaults; CPU contract tests cover the boundaries, but no full-model accuracy A/B is claimed for either model.

BailingLinear resolves its optional AWQ provider only when AWQ weights are loaded, so ordinary model construction does not require `vllm`. The Kimi constructor fixture declares the routing selector explicitly.

Requested-backend reads remain where they select a method, allocate compatible shapes or establish model-wide policy.

## CI fixture repair

Current head: `4275a5026050615139c3658a72b6a7d05d65b17f`.

The DeepSeek dual-stream test fixture now declares its native runner, BYPASSED TopK format and static expert dispatch policy. The production routing guard remains intact. This repairs the missing `topk` error in the registered CUDA graph test.

Validation: the original fixture reproduced the reported error at both the lower and upper PR production revisions. The corrected full test passed on one H200 GPU at both revisions, including opcheck, fullgraph compilation and CUDA graph capture/replay for replicated and non-replicated shared outputs. The tested fixture bytes match this commit. Applicable pre-commit checks passed.

GPU environment: Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, sgl-kernel 0.4.7 and FlashInfer 0.6.18. The test substitutes small CUDA operations for expert kernels; model loading, MoE numerical accuracy and full CI were not rerun for this fixture repair. Earlier validation below remains tied to its stated revisions.

## Earlier validation after rebase

Head: `fc2dd3d90bf86fe1b61741c1bb8d28a4e121dc8a`. Rebased onto main `553836c1647b3bfbeb266b49d76ec2c9df012425`; base `cheng/hot-fix/server-args-positional-api` is `77300dcce02c0b20d68cbc687bb56b54c4a97ace`.

- At this exact head, 6 focused CPU module(s) passed: 53 tests plus 85 reported subtests. Across all four PR heads, 15 focused modules completed 482 test executions plus 347 reported subtests, all passing.
- Each PR's full incremental tree matches the pre-rebase change applied to its rewritten base, retaining prior merge-only integration fixes. The stack remains #44480 -> #44991 -> #44993 -> #44994.
- Configured pre-commit checks passed over all 152 changed files in the full stack. Strict registration/entrypoint checks passed: 2,478 files / 3,012 registrations. CPU tests used Python 3.12.15 and Torch 2.14.1+cu130 with GPUs hidden.

GPU, full-model accuracy/throughput and full CI were not rerun for this rebase. Prior hardware measurements below remain evidence for their named earlier revisions; checked CUTLASS/Marlin/GGUF consumer sources are unchanged, which is source evidence rather than a new GPU run.

## Previous validation (before rebase)

Previous head: `b37b73a1ae1bdf3d73b6108deb76a14679a079b4`, based on #44991 and main `693d33330647c57f82e09ac39a34122fa46b5763`.

- At this exact head, 4 focused CPU modules passed: 28 tests plus 48 reported subtests, covering model policy constructors, shared scaling, ModelOpt dispatch and FP8 ownership. The full StandardDispatcher module also passed 21 tests plus 45 subtests on source bytes verified against this commit.
- The same new tests fail against the previous production sources for the intended missing scale, non-normalized shared compensation, model admission and dual-stream conditions. Compressed FP8/NVFP4 cases use real scheme/FusedMoE construction, TopK and dispatch with unit/nonunit factors and both renormalization choices. Model policy tests control FP8 quantization/native-provider boundaries; these CPU checks do not execute native quantized GEMMs.

## Motivation

A storage backend learns its host pools from a burst of hooks: the anchor pool through `register_mem_pool_host`, then every pool of the host pool group through `register_mem_host_pool_v2` — but nothing told the backend when the burst was over. A backend that must finalize once the pool set is known (e.g. register the instance with a remote cache manager whose spec cannot be amended after registration) had no correct moment to act and could only defer that work to the first data-path call, paying seconds of setup on the first request and surfacing config errors (manager unreachable, instance conflict) after startup instead of failing it.

## Modifications

- `HiCacheStorage` gains a no-op `on_host_pools_registered()`: fires exactly once per attach, right after the last call of the initial burst; pools registered later (dynamic draft sidecars) arrive through v2 alone and do not re-fire it. Raising fails the attach.
- The burst ends in different places on the two controllers, so each fires the hook at its own end: the base controller right after the anchor pool, `HybridCacheController` — whose per-pool v2 loop runs after `super().attach_storage_backend()` returns — after that loop. A `_registers_host_pools_after_super_attach` flag tells the two apart; no signatures change and no code moves.
- The hook defaults to a no-op, so existing backends are unaffected.
- Documents the registration lifecycle in `hicache_design.mdx`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (no model output changes). New CPU unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_storage_registration_hook.py`: the hybrid hook fires after its v2 burst exactly once, the base hook fires right after the anchor pool, base-path hook failure rolls the attach back, hybrid-path failure propagates, dynamic sidecars do not re-fire the hook.

items.body:
## Motivation

`python/sglang/kernels/README.md` says to classify kernels by the computation they perform, not by the model that first used them, and never to add a model bundle as a top-level group. An audit of current main found that this had drifted:

- `ops/muse_spark/` (#44665) was a model-named top-level group. It contained 22 files mixing norms, routing, GEMMs, collectives and reductions, with no KernelSpecs and no kernel tests. It had been added to `_GROUPS`, which is the only thing the guard test checked, so the test did not catch it.
- `attention/dsv4/` and `attention/dsa/` had collected quantization kernels, KV-cache stores and copies, a split-K GEMV, collective attention-residual kernels, runtime controllers and config predicates, and test oracles.
- Elsewhere, ops sat in the wrong group: GEMMs in `quantization`, RMSNorms in `elementwise`, attention metadata in `kvcache`, a forwarding shim in `attention/utils.py`, and the same computation implemented in two or three groups.

This PR fixes all of it in one pass. It writes the classification rules into the README and the `kernel-organization` skill, and makes the guard test enforce the README.

## Classification rules (README + skill)

- RoPE, including standalone RoPE and position ids, stays in `attention`.
- **Producer + output quantization belongs to the producer's group:**
  - norm + quant → `layernorm`
  - activation + quant → `activation`
  - a GEMM with a quant epilogue → `gemm`
  - MoE dispatch + quant → `moe`
  - `quantization` holds only pure format conversion: quant, dequant, scale layout, repack.
- **Any kernel that performs a cross-rank collective, or reads or writes peer memory, → `communication`**, whatever compute it fuses. Workspaces, symmetric buffers and process groups stay in `srt/layers/communication/`.
- **`kvcache` owns ops that read or write KV-cache contents:** store, gather, copy, quantize-into-cache, clear rows.
- **`attention` owns the index, shape and schedule tables attention kernels consume:** page tables, cu_seqlens, kv_indices, schedule metadata.
- A fused compute+store op stays with its compute group.
- `kda_kernels/` and `cake_kernels/` are documented as the agent-generated kernel backends. They are deliberately left in place, and new agent kernels keep landing there.

**Guard test** (`test_kernels_namespace.py`):
- The README group list must equal `_GROUPS`.
- The README Layout must list exactly the packages under `sglang/kernels/`.

Both checks fail on main.

## Modifications

All relocations are `git mv` plus import updates. Every moved function, class and constant was checked to be byte-identical apart from import paths, either by AST comparison or by a normalized diff. Relocation commits are kept apart from semantic commits. No forwarding shims remain: 94 old module paths have zero references anywhere.

### `ops/muse_spark` dissolved
- **layernorm:** `muse_spark_norm_gate{,_jit,_helion}`, `muse_spark_norm_residual{,_jit}`, `muse_spark_rmsnorm_nvfp4_quant{,_helion}`, `_muse_spark_tuning`.
- **attention:** `muse_spark_qk_norm_rope_store{,_helion}`.
- **moe:** `muse_spark_routing{,_jit}`, `muse_spark_post_expert_finalize_triton`.
- **communication:**
  - `muse_spark_all_gather`, `muse_spark_all_gather_norm_residual`
  - `muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce{,_cutedsl,_helion}`
  - SP `cutlass_all_gather_gemm`, `cutlass_gemm_reduce_scatter`, `sp_collective_gemm` (moved from `gemm`)
- **elementwise:** `row_sum`. **gemm:** `muse_spark_router_gemm`. It is kept but still unused; the model only reads its `MAX_TOKENS` threshold.
- **Helion runtime:** → `kernels/jit/utils/helion_runtime.py`.
- **Runtime state → `srt/layers/communication/`:** the GEMM+all-gather composition and projection workspace, `FinalizePushWorkspace`, and the SP collective-GEMM symmetric-memory workspace. The SP kernels now take the workspace as an argument.
- **The model calls the all-gather+norm op directly.** The removed `forward_with_ag` used to route it, and the norm op no longer imports srt model classes.
- **New coverage:** KernelSpecs for every entry point, plus 6 kernel test files (fused vs native). `triton_sum` → `sglang.test.kernels`, used as the `row_sum` bitwise reference.

### DeepSeek V4 / DSA
- **To `quantization`:**
  - `act_quant` (Triton and TileLang)
  - `fp8_group_major_quant_ue8m0` (was `dsv4/fp8_wo_a`)
  - `fp4_fake_quant` (was `dsv4/torch_quant`)
  - `quantize_fp4_indexer_tensor`
  - `dsa_quant_k_cache` (returns new tensors; it never writes the cache)
- **To `kvcache`:**
  - request-window row copy, c128 draft-state cleanup
  - V4 main-KV and DSA index-K accessors
  - unified-KV scatter
  - FP4 index-K store and gather (CUDA and HIP)
  - the DSA fused index-K store
- **To `gemm`:** `dsv4_indexer_head_weights_hip`, a split-K GEMV.
- **To `communication`:** `attn_res_collective` (NVLS pull reduce-scatter, multicast all-gather).
- **Runtime code → srt:** `OnlineC128MTPController`, the unified-KV config gate, `Gfx950FusedIndexer`.
- **Launchers into the kernel modules:** the sparse-prefill and CP-interleave launchers now live there, so srt no longer imports private `@triton.jit` kernels.
- **Folder fixes:**
  - DSA-only files at the attention top level → `dsa/`
  - V4-only files → `dsv4/`; `nsa_triton_decode/` → `dsv4/triton_sparse_decode/`
  - `dsv4/elementwise.py` → `dsv4/norm_rope.py`
  - the V3.2-only Q indexer → `dsa/indexer_q.py`
- **Renames:**
  - same-named dequant functions → `*_dsa` / `*_dsv4`
  - kpool metadata functions → `*_kpool`
  - `_kv_splits_for_stream` → `kv_splits_for_stream` (public)
- **Test oracles → `sglang.test.kernels`.** The dead `triton_create_paged_compress_data` is deleted.

### kvcache ↔ attention, attention subpackages
- **To `attention`:** `kv_indices`, `trtllm_mha_page_table`, `trtllm_mha_graph_metadata`, `aiter_unified_page_table`, `fused_qk_rope_reshape_and_cache`, and the MLA Q/K prep from `cache_ops` (→ `mla_qk_prep.py`).
- **`attention/utils.py` forwarding re-exports removed.** 21 importers now import from the defining modules. The shuffle-5D store and gather → `kvcache/shuffle_5d_cache.py`. Two duplicate inventory specs dropped.
- **SGLang-written files moved out of the vendored `attention/fla/`:** 7 files → `attention/linear/`, and `kda_prefill_graph_track` → `mamba/`. `BailingLinearKernel` → its srt backend.
- **FA4 MLA SM100:** test and benchmark code moved out of the production module (`flash_fwd_mla_sm100.py`) into `test/manual/`.
- **MiniMax sparse:** the Gluon prefill moved from `srt/layers/attention/minimax_sparse_ops` → `kernels/ops/attention/minimax_sparse/`. Its `tests/` folder had never been collected and had stale imports; it is now in `test/registered`, with the slow autotune test nightly. The unused `naive/` references are deleted.
- **Lazy KernelSpecs** for unregistered public entry points: Helion/CuTeDSL/PTX KDA and GDN, FP8 FA SM120, vattn asm, minimax sparse and CP indexer, and others.

### Other groups
- **GEMMs out of `quantization` → `gemm`:** `nvfp4_gemm_swiglu_nvfp4_quant`, the gfx950 MXFP8 GEMV/GEMM (with its tuning JSON), `mxfp8_flydsl`, `mxfp8_aiter`, and the MXFP8 blockscaled linears.
- **By rule 3:**
  - `rmsnorm_fake_quant_amd_gfx95` → `layernorm`
  - SwiGLU/SiLU+MXFP8 → `activation`
  - `minimax_quant_ue8m0` → `moe`
  - `upscale` (dequant) → `quantization`
  - MXFP8 epilogue helpers → `quantization`
  - `quant_store_kv_mxfp8` and the interleaved SF → `kvcache`
  - diffusion modulate+MXFP8 → `diffusion/modulate`
- **`elementwise`:** RMSNorms → `layernorm`; `gelu_and_mul_triton` and `bias_gelu` → `activation`.
- **Other moves:**
  - `hc_mix` split-K → `gemm`; `router_gate_matvec` → `gemm`
  - `silu_and_mul_clamp` / `silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant` → `activation`; these also serve dense MLPs.
  - `ngram_embedding` → `embeddings`
  - `softcap_row_argmax` → `sampling`
  - `bmm_fp8`'s implementation moved out of srt into `gemm/flashinfer_bmm_fp8.py`
  - `communication/mp.py` → `srt/distributed`
- **Duplicates:**
  - `moe/triton_sigmoid_gate_mul` merged into `elementwise.fused_sigmoid_mul`: bit-exact over 92 cases on sm_90/sm_100/sm_120.
  - Kept, each with a one-line comment saying why, because they are not bit-exact with their twin: `mla_output_gate` (rounds the gate to bf16 first), the `hc_mix` split-K vs persistent kernels, `swiglu_oai_mxfp8`, DSpark `SoftmaxTemp`, `act_quant`, the V4 Triton RoPE, the grok/gfx1250 RMSNorms, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU.
- **Housekeeping:**
  - hipcc build helpers → `kernels/jit/utils/hipcc.py`
  - `_jit_*` module prefixes removed
  - KernelSpecs added for `kv_canary` / `lplb`
  - `mhc.hc_combine` → `mhc_combine` (it clashed with `elementwise.hc_combine`)
  - test helpers `fp8_cvt` and `scatter_req_token_ids` reference → `sglang.test.kernels`
  - the unused `mxfp4_marlin_repack` deleted
  - CODEOWNERS kept in sync for moved files

items.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-hierarchical-cache` (write_through) the unified radix cache backs up every new tree node to host. After #39050 the D2H submits are merged per step, but the per-node bookkeeping that precedes a submit still runs inside `cache_finished_req`, on the scheduler thread, at the moment the node is inserted: `build_backup_spec` (SWA/Mamba transfer lists, `torch.cat`/`clone`), host pool `alloc` for KV + side pools (with SWA host eviction when that pool is full), `resolve_host_transfers`, `commit_backup`, `inc_lock_ref`, and the ack bookkeeping. On Inkling-Small-NVFP4 that is ~0.2 ms per node, and most of it is fixed per-call torch-op and Python overhead on small tensors, not per-token work.

## Modifications

Write-through backups are now queued at insert and backed up in merged batches at flush. There is no flag. Write-back, the buffer pipeline and the external linker keep their existing paths.

## Accuracy Tests

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base upstream/main 70f0b7351e vs this PR, TP=4, Rust tree core (the default). Workload: 128 lanes x 16 timed turns, multi-turn (a 1k-token prefix shared by every 16 lanes, 4-5.6k-token first prompt, +256 tokens per turn, outputs 128-512 with `ignore_eos`). The working set stays on device, so L2 only adds the write-through cost (no host hits). Each round runs L1 (main), L2 (main) and L2 (PR) servers back to back in a rotated order; loss is relative to the same round's L1, and the PR column is paired against main L2 per round. The numbers were taken with the batched path enabled on the PR's earlier heads (e7fa154960 / feae6173cd), which run the same write-through code as this head.

| host / model (recipe) | rounds | L2 loss vs L1, main | L2 loss vs L1, PR | PR vs main L2, paired |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4x B300, Inkling-Small-NVFP4 (Long Context: MXFP8 KV) | 5 | 1.63% | **0.80%** | +0.85% (t=3.1) |
| 4x GB300, Inkling-Small-NVFP4 (Long Context: MXFP8 KV) | 3 | 2.59% | **1.33%** | +1.29% (t=17.6) |
| 4x H200, Inkling-Small-NVFP4 (H200 recipe; TP=4 instead of its TP=8) | 3 | 0.68% | **0.41%** | +0.27% (t=3.4) |
| 4x B300, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (B300 FP4 low-latency) | 5 | 1.96% | 0.93% | +1.06% (t=2.1) |
| 4x GB300, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (GB300 FP4 low-latency) | 6* | 1.96% | 1.22% | +0.42% (t=0.9) |
| 4x H200, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 (H200 FP8 low-latency) | 5 | L2 1-2% faster than L1 | same | -0.04% (t=-0.08) |
| 1x H200, Qwen3-8B (server defaults, 64 lanes) | 3 | 2.84% | 2.69% | +0.15% (t=3.4) |

\* Round 1's L1 server ran before the FlashInfer autotune cache settled and is left out of the loss columns (n=5); the paired column uses all 6 rounds.

Inkling and DSV4 use `--max-total-tokens 2097152` (Inkling also `--max-mamba-cache-size 1024`), DSV4 `--hicache-ratio 2`. The PR helps where the request-finish bookkeeping is on the critical path (Inkling on Blackwell) and is neutral elsewhere: DSV4 runs at ~3k tok/s with a run-to-run spread larger than its L2 cost, and the H200 Qwen3-8B L2 cost is dominated by the page-size-1 host copy path, which this PR does not touch. An earlier GB300 session with the same commits (7 vs 7 interleaved L2 servers) measured +1.25% (t=3.2); its per-step profile shows the backup path 0.50 -> 0.30-0.33 ms and `process_batch_result` -0.22 to -0.27 ms, and the largest remaining L2 cost is `check_hicache_events` (0.77-0.89 ms per step).

## Motivation

When attention TP > 1, `MqaAttentionBase._local_attn_sink()` builds a padded, TP-local copy of `attn_sink` (`_attn_sink_local`) on the first forward, and never refreshes it afterwards. Online weight updates (e.g. `update_weights_from_tensor` in RL) write new values into `attn_sink`, but `MQALayer.forward()` keeps reading the stale copy. As a result, the model silently serves the startup sinks; with `load_format=dummy`, the sinks stay dummy for the whole run.

- Record the head slice used to build the copy, and add `MqaAttentionBase.refresh_attn_sink_cache()`. It copies the updated `attn_sink` slice into the existing `_attn_sink_local` in place.
- Call it from `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.post_load_weights()`, next to `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache()`.

items.title: [kernel] Fix cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration when num_tokens=0 in activation kernels
items.body:
## Summary

- Fix crash with `cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration` (error 9) when activation kernels (`silu_and_mul`, `gelu_tanh_and_mul`, `gelu_and_mul`, `gelu_quick`) are called with zero-row input tensors (`num_tokens=0`)
- Add early return guard for `num_tokens==0` to avoid launching CUDA kernels with invalid `dim3(0)` grid dimension

## Problem

In DeepEP expert-parallel deployments (e.g., DeepSeek V3, EP=8), when the batch size is small, some ranks may receive 0 tokens for all local experts. The MoE contiguous GEMM path then calls these activation functions with `(0, N*2)` shaped tensors, triggering the crash.

The error is sticky - it corrupts CUDA runtime state and causes subsequent unrelated CUDA operations to fail.

## Fix

```cpp
if (num_tokens == 0) return;
```

Added to the four affected functions in `sgl-kernel/csrc/elementwise/activation.cu`.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified with minimal reproduction script (num_tokens=32 works, num_tokens=0 no longer crashes)
- [ ] Real DeepEP deployment test (EP=8, small batch prefill)

Fixes #23609
